claim_register.claim: Strategic rule maintenance is ringfenced. Rules require maker/checker control, UAT testing, and approval before production setup. Proposals identify purpose, scope, and entity/counterparty impact. MT reviews the rule. After MT approval, eOPS requests DataOps setup. UAT amendments return to MT. Record MT approval dates in the DOI. MT or delegate reviews every rule annually; record reviewer and date. Consider payment failure, reconciliation breaks, NSTP volume, and STP effects when removing controls.

claim_register.claim: Fields form AND conditions; grouping supports complex rules. Creation requires a reason; comments are optional. New rules require checker approval, except dry-run rules. Dry-run rules do not execute immediately. Maker and checker must differ for creation and update. Authorized operators can disable live rules immediately. They can activate a live dry-run rule immediately for subsequent trade/cashflow processing. Updates require a reason and checker approval or rejection. Users can inspect history, export rules, and filter rule fields.

claim_register.claim: Cashflow suppression prevents downstream delivery and generates neither payment nor settlement accounting. Create suppression rules only when they avoid payment failure and reconciliation breaks. Addition and deletion require different maker/checker persons. Swift suppression prevents Swift/payment in Razor; listed maintenance profiles are `FMO_BR_APR`, `FMO_BR_MKR`, `FMO_OPS`, and `FMO_OPS_SUP`. These roles are source-specific and do not establish current entitlements. The source excludes legacy FX/equity rule maintenance from its strategic scope. Its China Day 1 auto-netting scope excludes that capability and requests a VD-1 enhancement.
